purpose: Qualify the isolated A/B runner and deterministic scorer before the full pilot.

cases.prompt: Read input/plan.md. Stress-test the plan for a go/no-go meeting. Rank the few assumptions that can kill it, say what evidence can be obtained this week, and end with a clear next action. Use only facts in the file. Do not browse, edit files, or invent evidence. Keep the answer under 900 words.

files.input/plan.md:
# Pilot plan: MeetPilot

We will launch an AI meeting assistant in six weeks with two engineers. It records Zoom sales calls, transcribes them, writes CRM notes, and charges $49 per seat. We heard enthusiasm in three calls with our own sales team; no external customer has used a prototype. The $49 price copies a competitor's public price. We promise one-click Zoom installation, but have not started Zoom Marketplace review. Raw audio and transcripts will be stored for 12 months. Security, consent, data residency, deletion, and legal review are not yet assigned. Success is 1,000 paid seats by day 30. Two design partners said they would try it, but neither signed a paid commitment.

cases.prompt: Read input/story.md and produce executable acceptance-test scenarios. Cover the main path, authorization, boundaries, failures, retry behavior, and recovery. Every scenario needs starting state, actor, steps, and observable expected results. Do not browse or edit files. Keep the answer under 1,100 words.

files.input/story.md:
# Invite a workspace member

As a workspace admin, I want to invite a teammate by email so they can join my workspace.

Acceptance rules:
- Only an admin may invite.
- Trim and lowercase email before checking uniqueness within the same tenant.
- A pending invite expires exactly 72 hours after creation.
- Resending creates a new token and immediately invalidates the old token.
- If the email provider fails, no active member may be created; a retry with the same idempotency key must not create duplicates.
- One admin may create at most five invites in a rolling hour.
- A revoked invite must always be rejected.

cases.prompt: Read input/evidence.md. Prepare a concise shipping-readiness evidence pack for the release owner. Keep local, CI, deployment, live access, approval, rollback, and provenance as separate claims. State go/no-go and the smallest actions needed to unblock it. Do not browse, edit files, or infer missing success. Keep the answer under 900 words.

cases.prompt: Read input/context.md and define a decision-ready product metrics dashboard. Give exact metric definitions, source events, time windows, guardrails, targets, alert owner/channel/response time, layout, and review cadence. Flag unavailable data instead of inventing current values. Do not browse or edit files. Keep the answer under 1,100 words.

files.input/context.md:
# FlowForge metrics context

FlowForge helps five-or-more-person teams automate recurring approval workflows. The decision is whether onboarding changes improve durable team value without causing failed runs. Available events: workspace_created(workspace_id, plan, at), member_invited(workspace_id, user_id, at), workflow_published(workspace_id, workflow_id, at), workflow_run_finished(workspace_id, workflow_id, status, duration_ms, at), subscription_started(workspace_id, mrr, at), subscription_cancelled(workspace_id, at), support_ticket_opened(workspace_id, severity, at). We do not yet collect satisfaction surveys or acquisition cost. A workspace is meaningfully active in a week only if at least three distinct published workflows finish successfully. Signups alone are considered vanity.
